requirements.requirement: Create an opsbot account on node1 (and correspondingly on node2 as the SSH target)
requirements.summary: adduser -D created opsbot on both node1 and node2; getent passwd and /etc/shadow entries confirm uid=1001 account exists with home/.ssh (0700) directory on both nodes.

requirements.requirement: opsbot has SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2, initiated from node1
requirements.summary: Ed25519 keypair generated as opsbot on node1 and its public key installed into node2's opsbot authorized_keys. After discovering and correcting a shadow-lock issue blocking pubkey auth, a live SSH command execution (whoami/hostname/id) from opsbot@node1 to opsbot@node2 succeeded, and was re-verified after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on both systems (password auth rejected)
requirements.summary: A 'Match User opsbot' sshd_config block enforcing AuthenticationMethods publickey was added, syntax-validated, and reloaded on both nodes. Explicit password-only SSH attempts against opsbot were tested in both directions (node1->node2 and node2->node1) and rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)'; node2 auth log corroborates an accepted pubkey login alongside a rejected password/locked attempt.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence for node1 and node2
requirements.summary: Both nodes show a full transition: pre-restart boot_id and healthy state, a background reboot acknowledgement, transient unreachability, a changed boot_id on return (node1 b83fd7ec->c386409c, node2 5e3bb0d6->8cd8ce3d, matching the fixed after-executor snapshot), and recovered sshd/account/key/config/cluster-SSH state verified post-restart for both nodes.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all three material outcomes of the task: opsbot was created on node1 (and node2), opsbot@node1 has working SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2, and key-only authentication (password rejected) was enforced and verified on both nodes in both directions. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly for both nodes, with boot-identity changes matching the fixed after-executor snapshot and full post-restart recovery of the account, key, sshd config, and cross-node SSH functionality. No unexplained or unnecessary mutations were found; the single non-obvious mutation (shadow lock-field change) was a necessary, well-evidenced fix.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before_prepare/after_executor diff, which shows only expected changes (boot identity, ephemeral ports, /tmp/reboot.log).

Password-rejection tests relied on client-side PreferredAuthentications=password/PubkeyAuthentication=no combined with server-side AuthenticationMethods publickey; the server's own offered-methods behavior was not separately captured via -v verbose output, though the auth log and Match block evidence corroborate publickey-only enforcement.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace clearly to the task outcome or the restart protocol. The account-locking correction (shadow field '!' -> '*' on both nodes) was a legitimate, evidence-supported fix for pubkey auth being blocked by the default locked account, not an unnecessary mutation. Failed initial adduser/ssh attempts were non-destructive discovery/retry steps with no lasting negative effect. The only residue is a trivial /tmp/reboot.log artifact left on both nodes from the reboot command's own output redirection - bounded, expected from the restart protocol, and not a security or functional concern.
